game_events#ge1.description: KXNHLOVERTIME and KXNHL2OT rules are one sentence ('go to overtime' / 'go to double overtime'): silent on whether reaching OT is defined by the OT faceoff, and on postponement, suspension or cancellation handling, unlike KXNHLOT's explicit 48h clause.
game_events#ge1.what_would_resolve: Kalshi rulebook entries for these two series or a listed market's full secondary rules text.

game_events#ge2.description: Whether tied games late are played for the guaranteed point (lower attempt share) is a hypothesis; published evidence is mixed and the magnitude relative to ordinary variance is unknown.
game_events#ge2.what_would_resolve: Measure tied-late attempt share against matched earlier tied minutes across 10 seasons with stakes interaction.

game_events#ge3.description: Playoff 5v5 overtime has only a few hundred games, too few for stable team-pair hazard; team-specific values will be shrunk heavily and may carry no information.
game_events#ge3.what_would_resolve: Pool playoff and regular-season tied-state 5v5 minutes and test predictive power out of sample.

game_events#ge4.description: The play-by-play situationCode field that encodes goalie-in-net for 6v5 identification is assumed from memory of the NHL API; early-season coverage is unchecked.
game_events#ge4.what_would_resolve: Download one 2016-17 and one 2025-26 play-by-play JSON and confirm the field and values.

game_events#ge5.description: The league-wide regulation tie rate is a drifting base rate (rule changes, scoring level, 3v3 introduction) and the baseline used in the record is not sourced to a season-by-season table; season-to-season drift of the tie rate is not yet an explicit input.
game_events#ge5.what_would_resolve: Compute the regulation tie rate per season from NHL results since 2005-06 and test drift against league goals per game before fixing any base rate.

game_events#ge6.description: Team-specific opening-ten-minute goal rates rest on about 13-14 team-hours per season, so persistent team effects beyond overall xG rates may be indistinguishable from noise; the size of the early-penalty contribution to the window is asserted, not measured.
game_events#ge6.what_would_resolve: Estimate split-half reliability of team window rates across seasons and the share of window goals scored on the power play since 2015-16.

game_moneyline_puckline#ml1.description: KXNHLGAME and KXNHLSPREAD never state whether shootout wins count or how a shootout margin is scored; the official-score reading (winner credited one goal) is assumed. Strike construction beyond 2.5 is untested. The same-league KXNHLTOTAL/KXNHLTEAMTOTAL rules do record a shootout winner as one extra goal, which is corroborating but not conclusive for these two series.
game_moneyline_puckline#ml1.what_would_resolve: Observe the first shootout settlement of a KXNHLSPREAD 0.5/1.5 rung or ask Kalshi to confirm.

game_moneyline_puckline#ml3.description: Which public xG model to use is unsettled: MoneyPuck, Natural Stat Trick and Evolving-Hockey differ in features and calibration, and vendor model changes alter history.
game_moneyline_puckline#ml3.what_would_resolve: Compare out-of-sample goal-difference prediction of each vendor xG on 5 seasons and record vintages.

game_moneyline_puckline#ml4.description: Home-ice advantage in the NHL has shifted over time and last-change effects are uncertain; whether a constant or team-specific home edge is appropriate is unresolved.
game_moneyline_puckline#ml4.what_would_resolve: Estimate home goal-difference by team with partial pooling over 15 seasons.

game_moneyline_puckline#ml5.description: KXNHLSERIES (playoff series winner) is owned by season_futures; its recovered rules ('If the Montreal Canadiens win the ... 2nd Round series') settle on the series result, so the per-game win model built here is only an upstream component whose use there (home pattern, goalie volatility) must be checked in that record.
game_moneyline_puckline#ml5.what_would_resolve: Cross-check season_futures stage s4 uses the same per-game win-probability engine as this archetype's stages s1-s4.

game_moneyline_puckline#ml6.description: nhl.lineup_impact_delta lists HockeyViz impact as a free source, but HockeyViz is a visual product, not a documented data feed; the free path is own RAPM from NHL shiftcharts, whose public field coverage and update timing are unverified here.
game_moneyline_puckline#ml6.what_would_resolve: Pull a sample of NHL shiftcharts for 20 games, confirm player-level on-ice intervals, and build a reference RAPM; drop HockeyViz as a data source unless an export exists.

game_moneyline_puckline#ml7.description: The probability that an empty-net goal converts a one-goal lead past 3:00 into a two-goal margin is stated in this record only as a rough range and is not sourced; it varies with pull time, team 6v5 strength and lead state.
game_moneyline_puckline#ml7.what_would_resolve: Estimate from play-by-play since 2015-16 the share of one-goal leads at 3:00 left that end with an empty-net goal, by team and coach.

game_total_and_team_total#tt1.description: No catalog input represents coach-level tempo and lead-protection style for totals; coach effects on pace beyond team ratings are unquantified and may be confounded with roster.
game_total_and_team_total#tt1.what_would_resolve: Estimate coach fixed effects on attempts and shot quality using coaching changes as natural experiments.

game_total_and_team_total#tt3.description: Referee-pair assignments are assumed available in NHL game summary reports, with crew announced the morning of the game; timing of public availability is unchecked.
game_total_and_team_total#tt3.what_would_resolve: Check the game summary and the NHL referee assignments feed over a sample of games for the time of first publication.

game_total_and_team_total#tt4.description: Whether goal totals are positively correlated beyond what pace explains (shared game state) at high totals is unsettled; evidence for a two-component meltdown mixture is limited to small tail counts.
game_total_and_team_total#tt4.what_would_resolve: Compare tail calibration of mixture vs single negative binomial on 15 seasons of games with 9 or more goals.

game_total_and_team_total#tt5.description: KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOAL left this archetype for unreg:playoff_series_aggregate; the series-length pmf it needs (nhl.series_game_count_pmf) lives in that record, which should reuse this archetype's per-game total model with no shootout credit in playoffs.
game_total_and_team_total#tt5.what_would_resolve: Cross-check that the playoff_series_aggregate record composes per-game totals from this archetype's stages s1-s4.

game_total_and_team_total#tt6.description: Rules text for both series is read. Still unseen or unstated: the full strike ladder beyond the sampled 11.5 / 5.5 rungs, any playoff-specific wording (no shootout exists), a postponement clause for KXNHLTEAMTOTAL, and the sourced regular-season shootout rate that sets the +1 mass.
game_total_and_team_total#tt6.what_would_resolve: Capture several KXNHLTEAMTOTAL and playoff KXNHLTOTAL markets' full rules and compute shootout share per season from NHL results.

goalie_saves#gs1.description: The sampled rules do not say whether overtime saves count or whether shootout shots are excluded, nor how a goalie not dressed (scratch) is treated versus 'active but never enters'.
goalie_saves#gs1.what_would_resolve: Find a settled KXNHLSAVE market that went to OT and one with a scratched goalie and compare to the box score.

goalie_saves#gs2.description: The coach's pull policy (how many goals or what performance triggers a pull) is not recorded as data and has to be inferred from past pulls, a small sample per coach.
goalie_saves#gs2.what_would_resolve: Pool coaches into policy clusters and test predictive power of pull timing across seasons.

goalie_saves#gs3.description: That the NHL boxscore exposes goalie-level TOI, shots against and relief-entry time in a form sufficient to build the minutes distribution has not been checked for older seasons. The relief-entry time for the goalie may only be available from play-by-play rather than the boxscore, which is also unverified.
goalie_saves#gs3.what_would_resolve: Fetch a 2016-17 and a 2025-26 boxscore JSON and confirm the goalie stats fields.

goalie_saves#gs4.description: How strongly arenas differ in SOG recording after 2019-20 tracking is unknown; the draft assumes a primary role for a bias that may now be small.
goalie_saves#gs4.what_would_resolve: Fit the arena random effect on post-2020 data and compare with the pre-2020 effect.

offfield_markets#of1.description: Expansion announcements are extremely rare (a handful in 30 years), so a base rate or hazard model has almost no data; the governance-gate stage score maps to probability only by judgement.
offfield_markets#of1.what_would_resolve: Document each past expansion bid's timeline and fit a coarse stage model with wide uncertainty, or treat the market as unmodellable.

offfield_markets#of2.description: KXNHLNEXTTEAM's sample is 'before Nov 1, 2026', which has passed; it is unclear how rolling or later windows are listed, and what happens if a trade occurs and then the player is moved again inside the window.
offfield_markets#of2.what_would_resolve: Capture the next listed window and observe how multiple moves in one window settle.

offfield_markets#of3.description: The Board of Governors voting threshold for an expansion award and the timing of special sessions are assumed from memory and are not stated in the sampled KXNHLEXPANSION text.
offfield_markets#of3.what_would_resolve: Read the NHL constitution or Board of Governors announcements for the expansion approval vote rule.

offfield_markets#of4.description: Insider-report archives with timestamps and report types are not available as a public dataset and would have to be collected going forward, so credibility estimates will be thin initially.
offfield_markets#of4.what_would_resolve: Begin capturing insider posts now and backfill from social archives where possible.

offfield_markets#of5.description: The Lindsay vote-share question left with KXNHLLINDSAY (carried as aw8 in season_awards_and_stats). For this archetype: no public archive of GM-candidate interview reports or of player retirement statements with timestamps is known, so nhl.gm_candidate_pool and nhl.retirement_hazard_profile depend on own capture and on unverified historical reconstruction.
offfield_markets#of5.what_would_resolve: Check whether any archive (e.g. dated news search) supports back-filling GM-search and retirement reports since 2015.

offfield_markets#of6.description: KXNHLNEXTTEAM lacks trade-specific inputs beyond contract clauses: player trade demand or intent, team seller or buyer status and trade-deadline timing, and the sampled market is a finalized one with a lapsed window, so the multi-outcome partition (including Retires / No Team) is only partly seen.
offfield_markets#of6.what_would_resolve: Add a seller-status and deadline-timing input once an active next-team market with a future window is sampled and test it on past deadlines.

offfield_markets#of7.description: KXNHLNEXTGM is silent on interim or acting GM titles and on a hire announced but effective after the deadline; KXNHLRETIRE is silent on an announcement later reversed (un-retirement) and on what counts as 'announces' (agent statement versus player).
offfield_markets#of7.what_would_resolve: Kalshi clarification or settlement precedent for interim GMs and reversed retirements.

parlay_combo#pc1.description: No NHL combo or parlay series exists in the ledger, so leg void treatment, same-game versus cross-game structure, leg count and settlement timing are all unknown.
parlay_combo#pc1.what_would_resolve: Capture the rules text when a combo series lists and build the payoff map from it.

parlay_combo#pc2.description: How Kalshi prices multi-leg combos (market maker quote, request-for-quote, or a fixed formula) and whether the price is available as a time series is unverified.
parlay_combo#pc2.what_would_resolve: Read Kalshi's multivariate market documentation and observe a live example.

parlay_combo#pc3.description: The strength of tail dependence between win, total and star points legs is estimated from history, and whether it is stable across rule or style changes is unknown; copula family choice is untested.
parlay_combo#pc3.what_would_resolve: Compare joint log-likelihood across copula families over rolling seasons and test stability.

parlay_combo#pc4.description: Pregame knowledge of the joint lineup state at the time a combo trades is partial; confirmations arrive in the hours before puck drop and combos may trade before them.
parlay_combo#pc4.what_would_resolve: Archive lineup vintages and measure the information gap between combo trading windows and confirmations.

parlay_combo#pc5.description: Whether Kalshi NHL combos are same-game multi-leg products or cross-game/cross-sport collections of existing markets is unverified, so whether within-game dependence inputs (credit kernel, copula tail dependence, scenario tree) are required at all, or only leg marginals plus void and logical-relation rules, is unknown.
parlay_combo#pc5.what_would_resolve: Read the rules text and market metadata of an actual Kalshi combo or parlay series covering NHL legs; until then treat dependence inputs as conditional and the void payoff map as the only certain requirement.

period_markets#pm1.description: KXNHL1PBTTS has no markets or rules text, so own-goal handling, overtime irrelevance and whether it counts per team at least one goal are unseen.
period_markets#pm1.what_would_resolve: Capture the rules when it lists; until then it cannot be modelled to settlement.

period_markets#pm2.description: Whether referees systematically balance penalties within a game (and by how much) is debated; the size of the effect on later-period penalty counts is uncertain.
period_markets#pm2.what_would_resolve: Estimate the lagged penalty differential coefficient on 15 seasons with crew random effects.

period_markets#pm3.description: That NHL API play-by-play provides the first-shift line combination and a reliable shift chart for opening deployment has not been checked.
period_markets#pm3.what_would_resolve: Pull a sample game shiftcharts payload and confirm the first shift players.

period_markets#pm4.description: Team-specific second-period long-change effects have small per-team samples (about 80 games a year) so any team-level estimate may be noise.
period_markets#pm4.what_would_resolve: Test persistence of team second-period uplift across seasons; if near zero keep league constant.

period_markets#pm6.description: Whether skater fatigue on back-to-backs or after travel produces a late-period fade, beyond the backup-goalie channel, is not established; a period-specific rest effect may be indistinguishable from zero after goalie identity is controlled.
period_markets#pm6.what_would_resolve: Estimate the period-by-rest interaction on 2015-16 onward team-period data with goalie identity controlled and check significance and stability across seasons.

period_markets#pm7.description: Rules text now exists for all period series except KXNHL1PBTTS (TITLE_ONLY); the claims that Hockey-Reference and the NHL API give period-by-period scoring with running score for older seasons remain unchecked.
period_markets#pm7.what_would_resolve: Fetch rules for each title-only period series when markets list and sample period score fields from 2015-16 and 2025-26 NHL API boxscores.

period_markets#pm8.description: The recovered period rules cover postponement before start (48h, fair price) but are silent on a game suspended or abandoned after puck drop, i.e. whether a completed period settles while later-period markets go to fair price.
period_markets#pm8.what_would_resolve: Kalshi rulebook text on in-progress suspensions for NHL period markets.

player_h2h#hh1.description: No head-to-head series is listed, so tie treatment (push, No, fair price), the stats offered and the rule for a non-playing or injured player are unknown; each rule shifts the effective probability by several points. The whole input list for this archetype is provisional and must be re-reviewed against real rules text when a series lists; the share of tied pairs is a guess, not data.
player_h2h#hh1.what_would_resolve: Read the rules text of the first head-to-head series when it is listed and map each tie and non-participation rule to a payoff table.

player_h2h#hh2.description: Pair-type correlation estimates for same-line pairs rest on few pair-games per season and line combinations change often, so line-pair-specific dependence is noisy.
player_h2h#hh2.what_would_resolve: Pool by position-slot type (centre-wing, wing-wing, same PP unit) instead of by individual pair.

player_h2h#hh3.description: Whether the negative correlation of opposing players' counts from opposed script is detectable for shots on goal beyond the shared pace effect is unknown.
player_h2h#hh3.what_would_resolve: Estimate the correlation of opposing players' SOG residuals conditional on team volume across seasons.

player_h2h#hh4.description: PP unit assignments are assumed obtainable from line projection sites or reconstructed from shift data; the accuracy and timing of projected units has not been checked.
player_h2h#hh4.what_would_resolve: Compare projected PP units from Daily Faceoff with shift-derived units over a month of games.

player_h2h#hh5.description: The blueprint says only that player A records more of a stat than player B; it is unknown whether both players must be in the same game (pairs of teammates or opponents) or whether cross-game or multi-game comparisons exist, which would remove the dependence stage and the pair-type inputs.
player_h2h#hh5.what_would_resolve: Read the rules text of the first head-to-head series that lists and check the event definition and the pairing rule before any dependence input is treated as required.

player_h2h#hh6.description: nhl.ipp_by_state and nhl.sog_share_on_ice cite NHL API play-by-play for on-ice skaters; the API play-by-play events do not, to our knowledge, carry on-ice skater lists, so on-ice state needs a join with shiftcharts or HTML time-on-ice reports (same open question as pp3/sg5).
player_h2h#hh6.what_would_resolve: Pull one play-by-play JSON and its shiftcharts and test on-ice reconstruction at each event time; document join accuracy.

player_points_goals_assists#pp1.description: KXNHLANYGOAL has no markets or rules text so its treatment of empty-net, overtime and own goals and its relation to the N+ ladder are unseen; the ladder rules do not state whether overtime and empty-net goals count.
player_points_goals_assists#pp1.what_would_resolve: Capture rules when listed and compare with a settled market after an OT or EN goal.

player_points_goals_assists#pp3.description: That the NHL API play-by-play identifies on-ice skater ids for each event and goalie-pulled state in all seasons since 2012-13, which IPP and on-ice xG require, has not been confirmed.
player_points_goals_assists#pp3.what_would_resolve: Download sample play-by-play from several seasons and check fields for on-ice players.

player_points_goals_assists#pp4.description: Official NHL scoring credits (assists, goal attribution) can be corrected after the game; the rules do not name the data feed or the cut-off for corrections, so settlement timing risk exists. The sampled rules also name no feed as the source of truth for the ladder series, so the NHL box score as authority is an assumption.
player_points_goals_assists#pp4.what_would_resolve: Compare settled outcomes with box scores a day later for known scoring changes.

player_points_goals_assists#pp5.description: The rules say only that a player who is "active" but never enters the game settles to the last fair market price; "active" is undefined, and the treatment of a healthy scratch or a skater ruled out before the game (No, void or fair price) is not stated, so lineup-confirmation timing may be first-order for YES probability.
player_points_goals_assists#pp5.what_would_resolve: Find settled markets where a listed skater was a healthy scratch or injured out and compare settlement with the NHL box score and Kalshi resolution notice.

player_shots_on_goal#sg1.description: No Kalshi series exists for skater shots on goal, so settlement (OT counting, shootout exclusion, fair-price rule for non-playing skaters, ladder strikes) is inferred from sibling prop ladders and is unverified. Every audit verdict and the rung structure in this record are therefore conditional on the sibling-ladder assumption and must be re-checked when a series lists.
player_shots_on_goal#sg1.what_would_resolve: Read the rules text when a KXNHL shots series is first listed; until then keep the archetype provisional.

player_shots_on_goal#sg2.description: That the NHL stats API boxscore exposes per-player shots on goal and shot events with shooter and on-ice players for all seasons since 2012-13 is assumed, not checked.
player_shots_on_goal#sg2.what_would_resolve: Pull samples from boxscore and play-by-play endpoints for several seasons and inspect fields.

player_shots_on_goal#sg3.description: The strength of arena-level SOG recording bias after the introduction of puck and player tracking is unknown, so the venue input may be material or negligible.
player_shots_on_goal#sg3.what_would_resolve: Estimate the arena random effect separately before and after 2019-20.

player_shots_on_goal#sg4.description: Pass and shot-origin tracking data that would improve block and miss prediction (shot lane, defender position) is held by paid vendors and is not public.
player_shots_on_goal#sg4.what_would_resolve: License a tracking feed (Sportlogiq or Stats Perform) or test whether public location data suffice.

player_shots_on_goal#sg5.description: nhl.sog_share_on_ice and nhl.opp_sog_for_rate need shot events with the on-ice skater list; the NHL API play-by-play does not, to our knowledge, carry on-ice lists, which would require joining NHL shiftcharts or HTML time-on-ice reports by event time.
player_shots_on_goal#sg5.what_would_resolve: Pull one play-by-play JSON and the matching shiftcharts for the same game and test whether on-ice skaters can be reconstructed at each shot event time; record the join success rate.

season_awards_and_stats#aw1.description: KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS is titled 'Playoffs Goal Leader (by Round)' but only a Finals market is sampled: for earlier rounds it is unseen whether the leaderboard spans all series of the round or one series, and whether the text is silent on goals later rescinded by scoring changes.
season_awards_and_stats#aw1.what_would_resolve: Capture rules text for a first- or second-round KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS market.

season_awards_and_stats#aw10.description: Whether Kalshi applies the league tiebreak for Art Ross (more goals first, from memory) before its 1/N rule, and whether a shared Rocket Richard (which the league has awarded to tied players) pays 1/N, is not stated in the sampled rules (carried from season_futures sf8).
season_awards_and_stats#aw10.what_would_resolve: Ask Kalshi or verify on a settled tie; confirm the Art Ross tiebreak order on NHL.com.

season_awards_and_stats#aw2.description: The Jack Adams voting body and the ballot timing (end of regular season) are assumed from memory of the award; whether eligibility excludes coaches fired mid-season is not in the sampled text.
season_awards_and_stats#aw2.what_would_resolve: Check the NHL award description and past winners for mid-season coaching changes.

season_awards_and_stats#aw4.description: How strongly voters weight narrative versus points-based over-performance is unknown from a small history of winners, so the expectation-delta model could be mis-specified.
season_awards_and_stats#aw4.what_would_resolve: Fit alternative ranking models to 20 seasons of finalists and test out-of-sample calibration.

season_awards_and_stats#aw5.description: KXNHLMVP ('NHL Hart Memorial Trophy Winner') has no rules text and no listed markets and duplicates KXNHLHART; whether it is the same award, a different voting (e.g. a fan vote) or a retired series is unknown, so it is priced as Hart only by assumption.
season_awards_and_stats#aw5.what_would_resolve: Read KXNHLMVP rules when markets list and compare with KXNHLHART text.

season_awards_and_stats#aw7.description: MoneyPuck preseason projections and Elite Prospects or TSN consensus rankings are assumed to provide multi-season history for calibrating the coach expectation delta, and no mapping from that delta to a win probability among about 30 coaches is specified (award_vote_share_model is player-only); availability is unchecked.
season_awards_and_stats#aw7.what_would_resolve: Check whether historical preseason point projections exist for 10+ seasons and fit a coach-level conditional logit of Jack Adams winners on the delta.

season_awards_and_stats#aw8.description: Ted Lindsay results (voted by NHLPA members) are, to our knowledge, published as finalists and winner only, so award_vote_share_model cannot be fit on Lindsay vote shares; electorate and ballot facts are from memory (carried from offfield of5 after Lindsay was reassigned here).
season_awards_and_stats#aw8.what_would_resolve: Check NHLPA and NHL.com Lindsay pages for published vote totals; if absent, fit a rank-ordered model on finalists and winners only.

season_awards_and_stats#aw9.description: The award vote-share regression uses only finalists (a few dozen to about 100 rows per award over 20 seasons, mixed eras, selection by finalist status) with 8+ covariates, so it is overfit-prone and voter narrative is not specified (carried from season_futures sf7).
season_awards_and_stats#aw9.what_would_resolve: Fit with all vote-receiving players where published, few covariates and leave-one-season-out validation.

season_futures#sf1.description: Recovered rules for KXNHL, KXNHLEAST, KXNHLWEST, KXNHLPLAYOFF, KXNHLSERIES and KXNHL4NATIONS are one sentence each: silent on a cancelled or shortened season or tournament, a forfeited or unfinished series, and dead heats; settlement in those states is unknown.
season_futures#sf1.what_would_resolve: Kalshi rulebook text for NHL outrights, or a precedent settlement under a cancelled event.

season_futures#sf10.description: KXNHL4NATIONS calibration rests on a handful of best-on-best tournaments with different formats (Olympic, World Cup, 4 Nations); the per-game win-probability mapping from national-roster strength and the host-crowd term cannot be estimated reliably.
season_futures#sf10.what_would_resolve: Back-test the roster-strength model on 2014 Olympics, 2016 World Cup and 2025 4 Nations and report calibration with intervals.

season_futures#sf11.description: Streakiness of team results beyond strength (goalie hot streaks, schedule clustering) is weakly estimated; the lag-1 correlation of results controlling for strength may be near zero and dominates the longest-streak tail.
season_futures#sf11.what_would_resolve: Estimate lag-k correlation of residual results over 20 seasons and compare simulated league maxima with history.

season_futures#sf2.description: No input represents coach quality or coaching changes as a driver of team strength; it enters only through unstructured news and the effect is unquantified.
season_futures#sf2.what_would_resolve: Estimate coach effects from changes mid-season and decide whether a rating adjustment is warranted.

season_futures#sf3.description: The playoff officiating regime is only a flag; its effect on series outcomes (penalties and power plays differ in the playoffs) has no quantified input.
season_futures#sf3.what_would_resolve: Compare penalty counts and power-play shares in playoff games with the regular season and test their effect on series results.

season_futures#sf4.description: The NHL tiebreaker order for the worst record and for draft or Presidents' Trophy ties used by Kalshi (procedure for 'worst record') is not given in the sampled text, only that the league procedures apply.
season_futures#sf4.what_would_resolve: Confirm the league tiebreak for last place and compare with the Presidents' Trophy order stated in the sibling contract.

season_futures#sf5.description: The effect of preseason priors versus current data in the rating after only about 14 games is uncertain, and its size drives how much rating uncertainty must be injected into simulations.
season_futures#sf5.what_would_resolve: Backtest the prior weight at game 14 on 15 seasons using out-of-sample points and playoff qualification outcomes.

season_futures#sf6.description: KXNHLRECORDWORST is now the argmin of the simulated season totals (s5), but late-season tanking incentives created by draft-lottery odds (nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing) are not an input here, and their effect on the bottom-of-table points is unquantified.
season_futures#sf6.what_would_resolve: Measure post-deadline points-per-game shortfall of bottom-five teams versus their rating-implied rate across past seasons.

season_futures#sf7.description: The award vote-share regression (finalists only, a few dozen to about 100 rows per award, mixed eras, 8+ covariates) is overfit-prone; the award series were reassigned to season_awards_and_stats and this open question is carried there as aw9.
season_futures#sf7.what_would_resolve: Cap covariates at 3-4, use leave-one-season-out validation of winner rank across 20 seasons, and report calibration before using any vote-share probability.

season_futures#sf8.description: Whether a league tiebreak is applied before the $1/N rule for Art Ross and Rocket Richard is not stated in the sampled text; both series were reassigned to season_awards_and_stats and this question is carried there as aw10.
season_futures#sf8.what_would_resolve: Read the full rules text of KXNHLROSS and KXNHLRICHARD from live markets and a settled season-end example to see whether league tiebreaks are used.

season_futures#sf9.description: Division-winner series (ATLANTIC, METROPOLITAN, CENTRAL, PACIFIC) have empty secondary rules, so the tiebreak for a points tie is unstated, and KXNHLWSTREAK does not say whether overtime and shootout wins extend a winning streak or how streaks spanning the season start are counted.
season_futures#sf9.what_would_resolve: Ask Kalshi or observe a settled division/streak market with a tie or an OT-win streak; until then simulate under both readings and report the spread.

unreg:draft_selection#d1.description: Sampled rules for KXNHLDRAFTPICK and KXNHLDRAFTTOP give only the YES condition; they do not name a source of truth, say whether 'Nth overall' counts forfeited slots, or say what happens if the draft is postponed past expiry or a selection is ruled invalid.
unreg:draft_selection#d1.what_would_resolve: Read the full Kalshi rulebook/terms page for these series or a disputed-settlement notice covering forfeits and postponement.

unreg:draft_selection#d2.description: Current lottery mechanics (number of draws, maximum positions a club can rise, any limit on repeated wins) are quoted from general knowledge and may have changed since the last rule revision.
unreg:draft_selection#d2.what_would_resolve: Read the league's current lottery procedure page and confirm each rule against the most recent lottery results.

unreg:draft_selection#d3.description: Clubs' internal draft boards and need rankings are private; public rankings are the only board proxy, so club-specific preferences are inferred from past picks only.
unreg:draft_selection#d3.what_would_resolve: Compare out-of-sample accuracy of the inferred club preferences against actual picks over several drafts.

unreg:draft_selection#d4.description: Effect of the need profile versus best-available is contested in public work and may be near zero in the top five; its size by slot band is not established.
unreg:draft_selection#d4.what_would_resolve: Estimate the need coefficient by slot band on historical drafts and test whether it is distinguishable from zero.

unreg:draft_selection#d5.description: The exact current rule ordering playoff clubs in slots 17-28 (pure regular-season points versus a division-winner adjustment) is from memory; only slots 29-32 (conference-final losers, finalist, winner) are certain.
unreg:draft_selection#d5.what_would_resolve: Read the NHL's current draft-order procedure and check it against the 2024-2026 first-round orders.

unreg:draft_selection#d6.description: A multi-service public ranking history back to 2005 probably does not exist: McKeen's and FC Hockey are paywalled, the Elite Prospects draft guide is paid, McKenzie archives are patchy before about 2010. Calibration windows for the board model may be limited to ~2012 onward.
unreg:draft_selection#d6.what_would_resolve: Inventory archived final rankings per service per year and fix the calibration window to years with at least three services.

unreg:draft_selection#d7.description: Draft-week insider reports have no clean public archive, so insider_report_credibility and its interaction with GM reach tendency cannot be back-tested until the project captures reports across several drafts.
unreg:draft_selection#d7.what_would_resolve: Capture timestamped insider claims for at least three drafts and score them against actual picks.

unreg:draft_selection#d8.description: CapFriendly, the main free historical source for pick conditions and protections, shut down in July 2024; completeness of PuckPedia and Wayback snapshots for 2005-2024 pick conditions is unchecked.
unreg:draft_selection#d8.what_would_resolve: Sample 30 conditional picks from 2010-2024 and check whether PuckPedia or Wayback snapshots record their conditions and resolution.

unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p1.description: No sampled rule names the source of truth, says whether OT goals count toward KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOAL ('collectively score' implies yes), or covers an unfinished series or a named team that never reaches the championship series.
unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p1.what_would_resolve: Read the full Kalshi rulebook for these series or a past settlement of a series total with OT games.

unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p2.description: The sign and size of within-series game dependence (momentum vs bounce-back) and of elimination-state effects are estimated from small playoff samples; the 0-3 states have very few cases.
unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p2.what_would_resolve: Estimate the effects across 15+ playoff seasons with out-of-sample checks, reporting standard errors by state.

unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p3.description: Free endpoints for play-by-play and shift data are assumed to expose empty-net timing and pulled-goalie times back to 2010; field coverage by season has not been checked.
unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p3.what_would_resolve: Pull a sample of games from several seasons and check which fields are populated.

unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p4.description: KXNHL30COMEBACK is a league-wide union over up to 15 series rather than a single-series aggregate; it fits this archetype's sequence model but needs bracket simulation, and KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOALS (plural) is mentioned in the ledger narrative but absent from the live series.
unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p4.what_would_resolve: Confirm the comeback series is modelled here in the integrated catalog and check the ledger for the plural total-goals ticker and its rules.

unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p5.description: goalie_start_forecast in the catalog is built around regular-season rotation rules (back-to-backs, 3-in-4) that rarely apply in playoffs; a playoff-specific starter-change hazard after poor games is not defined.
unreg:playoff_series_aggregate#p5.what_would_resolve: Estimate P(starter change after a game with save percentage below a threshold) from 2005-06 onward playoff boxscores.

unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.description: The player-total rules state no minimum games, trade or retirement clause, do not say whether post-season scoring corrections after the last game are applied, and the two goal series (KXNHLPSEASONGOALS, KXNHLSEASONGOALS) may differ in wording beyond the sampled markets.
unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.what_would_resolve: Sample further markets from both goal series and KXNHLSEASONPPTS and read the full rules for correction cut-off and trade handling.

unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.description: The 'All-NHL team' contract type has no live series or rules text, so its voting body and selection process are unknown and nothing can be modelled for it.
unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.what_would_resolve: Wait for a listed series and collect its rules text.

unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.description: Shooting-percentage persistence for elite scorers is what decides 40+/60+ goal tails; whether a player's above-xG finishing over 2-3 seasons is skill or luck is weakly identified, so the shrinkage constant for nhl.finishing materially moves tail probabilities.
unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.what_would_resolve: Estimate split-half reliability of goals-minus-ixG for forwards with 500+ shots and set the shrinkage constant from it.

unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.description: That official NHL statistics treat shootout goals separately from player goal totals (so that they do not count toward a player's season goals) is assumed from league practice; the rules text does not mention it.
unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.what_would_resolve: Check a recorded shootout game in NHL stats and compare player goals.

unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.description: The NHL publishes no official injury feed, so the NHL API player status listed as a free source for the games-played hazard covariates is unverified; injury history beyond games missed comes from paid trackers (Man Games Lost) or scraped team reports.
unreg:team_and_player_season_counting#sc.what_would_resolve: Check what the NHL API player endpoints expose about injury status and compare with Man Games Lost coverage for 3 seasons.
